A concave lens $L_2$ of focal length $15\text{ cm}$ is placed coaxially to the right of $L_1$ such that the final image of the object is formed at infinity. The distance between the two lenses is _________ $\text{cm}$.

A concave lens $L_2$ of focal length $15\text{ cm}$ is placed coaxially to the right of $L_1$ such that the final image of the object is formed at infinity. The distance between the two lenses is _________ $\text{cm}$.

For the first lens $L_1$ (convex):
$u_1 = -40\text{ cm}$
$f_1 = +20\text{ cm}$
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-40} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{40}$
$\Rightarrow v_1 = +40\text{ cm}$

The intermediate image $I_1$ is formed $40\text{ cm}$ to the right of $L_1$. This image acts as an object for the second lens $L_2$.

For the second lens $L_2$ (concave):
The final image is formed at infinity, so $v_2 = \infty$.
$f_2 = -15\text{ cm}$
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\infty} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{-15}$
$\Rightarrow u_2 = +15\text{ cm}$

This means the object for $L_2$ (which is $I_1$) must be a virtual object located $15\text{ cm}$ to the right of $L_2$.
Since $I_1$ is $40\text{ cm}$ to the right of $L_1$ and $15\text{ cm}$ to the right of $L_2$, the distance between the two lenses is $d = 40 - 15 = 25\text{ cm}$.

All the curved surfaces of both lenses have the same radius of curvature of $30\text{ cm}$. If this entire combination is completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $1.8$, the equivalent focal length of the combination will be:
questions.question: A biconvex lens of refractive index $1.5$ and a biconcave lens of refractive index $1.2$ are placed in contact. All the curved surfaces of both lenses have the same radius of curvature of $30\text{ cm}$. If this entire combination is completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $1.8$, the equivalent focal length of the combination will be:
questions.solution:
For the biconvex lens, the radii of curvature are $R_1 = +30\text{ cm}$ and $R_2 = -30\text{ cm}$.
The focal length $f_1$ of the biconvex lens in the liquid of refractive index $1.8$ is given by:
$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_1}{\mu_m} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.8} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{-30}\right) = \left(\dfrac{5}{6} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{30}\right) = \left(-\dfrac{1}{6}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{15}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{90}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

For the biconcave lens, the radii of curvature are $R_1 = -30\text{ cm}$ and $R_2 = +30\text{ cm}$.
The focal length $f_2$ of the biconcave lens in the liquid is:
$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_2}{\mu_m} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \left(\dfrac{1.2}{1.8} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{-30} - \dfrac{1}{30}\right) = \left(\dfrac{2}{3} - 1\right)\left(-\dfrac{2}{30}\right) = \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{15}\right) = +\dfrac{1}{45}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The equivalent focal length $F_{eq}$ of the combination in the liquid is:
$\dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = -\dfrac{1}{90} + \dfrac{1}{45} = \dfrac{-1 + 2}{90} = \dfrac{1}{90}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

Thus, $F_{eq} = +90\text{ cm}$.

Answer: $+90\text{ cm}$

questions.q: A lens made of glass with a refractive index of $1.5$ has a certain focal length in air. When this lens is completely immersed in an unknown transparent liquid, its focal length becomes $2.5$ times its focal length in air. The refractive index of the unknown liquid is
questions.question: A lens made of glass with a refractive index of $1.5$ has a certain focal length in air. When this lens is completely immersed in an unknown transparent liquid, its focal length becomes $2.5$ times its focal length in air. The refractive index of the unknown liquid is
questions.solution:
Let the focal length of the lens in air be $f_a$ and in the liquid be $f_l$.

Using the Lens Maker's Formula for the lens in air:
$\dfrac{1}{f_a} = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

For the lens in the liquid, the relative refractive index is $\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l}$. The formula becomes:
$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Dividing the first equation by the second gives:
$\dfrac{f_l}{f_a} = \dfrac{\mu_g - 1}{\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1}$

We are given that $f_l = 2.5 f_a$ and $\mu_g = 1.5$. Substituting these values:
$2.5 = \dfrac{1.5 - 1}{\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} - 1}$

$2.5 = \dfrac{0.5}{\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} - 1}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} - 1 = \dfrac{0.5}{2.5} = 0.2$

$\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} = 1.2$

$\mu_l = \dfrac{1.5}{1.2} = \dfrac{15}{12} = 1.25$

Answer: $1.25$

questions.q: An astronomer wishes to improve the resolving power of an astronomical telescope to clearly distinguish two closely spaced binary stars. Which of the following modifications will successfully achieve this?
questions.question: An astronomer wishes to improve the resolving power of an astronomical telescope to clearly distinguish two closely spaced binary stars. Which of the following modifications will successfully achieve this?
options: Increase the wavelength of the incident light
Increase the focal length of the objective lens
Increase the diameter of the objective lens
Decrease the diameter of the objective lens
questions.solution:
The resolving power of an astronomical telescope is given by the relation:

$\text{Resolving Power} = \dfrac{D}{1.22\lambda}$

where $D$ is the diameter (aperture) of the objective lens and $\lambda$ is the wavelength of the incident light.

From this expression, the resolving power is directly proportional to the diameter of the objective lens and inversely proportional to the wavelength of light. Therefore, to increase the resolving power, one must increase the diameter of the objective lens. Changing the focal length affects magnifying power, not resolving power.

Answer: Increase the diameter of the objective lens

The object is placed to the left of $L_1$. The height of the final image formed by the system is _________ $\text{cm}$.

$f_1 = +20\text{ cm}$

The intermediate image $I_1$ is formed $60\text{ cm}$ to the right of $L_1$. Since the distance between the lenses is $45\text{ cm}$, $I_1$ lies $60 - 45 = 15\text{ cm}$ to the right of $L_2$.
This acts as a virtual object for $L_2$.

$f_2 = +10\text{ cm}$
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{10}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3+2}{30} = \dfrac{5}{30} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

It is observed that the light takes $0.5\text{ ns}$ longer to travel through the slab than it would take to travel the same distance in a vacuum. If the speed of light in vacuum is $3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, the refractive index of the glass slab is:
questions.question: A light pulse is sent through a glass slab of thickness $30\text{ cm}$. It is observed that the light takes $0.5\text{ ns}$ longer to travel through the slab than it would take to travel the same distance in a vacuum. If the speed of light in vacuum is $3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, the refractive index of the glass slab is:
questions.solution:
Let the thickness of the glass slab be $d = 30\text{ cm} = 0.3\text{ m}$.

The time taken by light to travel through the glass slab is $t_{\text{glass}} = \dfrac{\mu d}{c}$, where $\mu$ is the refractive index of the glass.

The time taken to travel the same distance in vacuum is $t_{\text{vac}} = \dfrac{d}{c}$.

The extra time taken is given by:
$\Delta t = t_{\text{glass}} - t_{\text{vac}} = \dfrac{\mu d}{c} - \dfrac{d}{c} = \dfrac{(\mu - 1)d}{c}$

Rearranging for $\mu$, we get:
$\mu - 1 = \dfrac{c \Delta t}{d}$

Substitute the given values ($c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, $\Delta t = 0.5 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s}$, $d = 0.3\text{ m}$):
$\mu - 1 = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8 \times 0.5 \times 10^{-9}}{0.3} = \dfrac{0.15}{0.3} = 0.5$

$\mu = 1 + 0.5 = 1.5$

Answer: $1.5$

In the first configuration, the objective lens is in air, the wavelength of light used is $600\text{ nm}$, and the semi-vertical angle of the cone of light entering the objective is $30^{\circ}$. In the second configuration, the objective is immersed in an oil of refractive index $1.5$, the wavelength of light used is $400\text{ nm}$, and the semi-vertical angle is $60^{\circ}$. The ratio of the limit of resolution in the first configuration to that in the second configuration is:
questions.question: A microscope operates in two different configurations to observe a specimen. In the first configuration, the objective lens is in air, the wavelength of light used is $600\text{ nm}$, and the semi-vertical angle of the cone of light entering the objective is $30^{\circ}$. In the second configuration, the objective is immersed in an oil of refractive index $1.5$, the wavelength of light used is $400\text{ nm}$, and the semi-vertical angle is $60^{\circ}$. The ratio of the limit of resolution in the first configuration to that in the second configuration is:
questions.solution:
The limit of resolution $x$ of a microscope is given by $x = \dfrac{1.22 \lambda}{2 \mu \sin\theta}$.

Thus, $x \propto \dfrac{\lambda}{\mu \sin\theta}$.

For the first configuration:
$\lambda_1 = 600\text{ nm}$, $\mu_1 = 1$, $\theta_1 = 30^{\circ}$
$x_1 \propto \dfrac{600}{1 \times \sin 30^{\circ}} = \dfrac{600}{0.5} = 1200$

For the second configuration:
$\lambda_2 = 400\text{ nm}$, $\mu_2 = 1.5$, $\theta_2 = 60^{\circ}$
$x_2 \propto \dfrac{400}{1.5 \times \sin 60^{\circ}} = \dfrac{400}{1.5 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \dfrac{1600}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Taking the ratio of the two limits of resolution:
$\dfrac{x_1}{x_2} = \dfrac{1200}{\dfrac{1600}{3\sqrt{3}}} = 1200 \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{1600} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times 3\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{9\sqrt{3}}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{9\sqrt{3}}{4}$

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ produces a virtual image of a real object. If the distance between the object and its virtual image is $45\text{ cm}$, the linear magnification produced by the lens is ________.
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ produces a virtual image of a real object. If the distance between the object and its virtual image is $45\text{ cm}$, the linear magnification produced by the lens is ________.
questions.solution:
For a virtual image formed by a convex lens, both the object and the image lie on the same side of the lens, with the image being further away.

Let the object distance be $u = -x$ (where $x > 0$).
The image distance is $v = -(x + 45)$.

Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

Substituting the values:
$\dfrac{1}{-(x + 45)} - \dfrac{1}{-x} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{x + 45} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{x + 45 - x}{x(x + 45)} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$\dfrac{45}{x^2 + 45x} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$x^2 + 45x - 900 = 0$

Solving the quadratic equation:
$(x + 60)(x - 15) = 0$

Since $x$ must be positive, $x = 15\text{ cm}$.
Thus, $u = -15\text{ cm}$ and $v = -60\text{ cm}$.

The linear magnification is:
$m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{-60}{-15} = 4$

Answer: $4$

questions.solution:
For a plano-convex lens, the principal axis is perpendicular to its plane surface.

When the lens is cut by a plane perpendicular to the principal axis, the cut is parallel to the existing plane surface.

This divides the lens into two pieces:
1. A piece with two parallel plane surfaces (a glass slab). Its radii of curvature are $R_1 = \infty$ and $R_2 = \infty$. Its power is $P_1 = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{\infty} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = 0$.

Thus, the powers of the two pieces are $P$ and $0$.

Answer: $P$ and $0$

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \dfrac{\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/2} = \sqrt{3}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{v} = \dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{1}{60} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{120} = \dfrac{1}{120}$

$-\dfrac{\mu_2}{v^2} \dfrac{dv}{dt} + \dfrac{\mu_1}{u^2} \dfrac{du}{dt} = 0$

Substituting the known values ($v_o = 2 \text{ mm/s}$):
$v_i = \dfrac{1}{1.5} \left(\dfrac{180}{-60}\right)^2 \times 2$

$v_i = \dfrac{2}{3} \times (3)^2 \times 2 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 9 \times 2 = 12 \text{ mm/s}$

$\dfrac{1}{64} = \dfrac{3}{16R}$

By the lens maker's formula in air:
$\dfrac{1}{f_a} = (\mu_L - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

When immersed in the liquid of refractive index $\mu_m$:
$\dfrac{1}{f_m} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_L}{\mu_m} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Dividing the two equations:
$\dfrac{f_m}{f_a} = \dfrac{\mu_L - 1}{\dfrac{\mu_L}{\mu_m} - 1}$

Given that $f_m = 4f_a$ and $\mu_m = \dfrac{4}{3}$:
$4 = \dfrac{\mu_L - 1}{\dfrac{3\mu_L}{4} - 1}$

$4\left(\dfrac{3\mu_L}{4} - 1\right) = \mu_L - 1$

$3\mu_L - 4 = \mu_L - 1$

$2\mu_L = 3$

$\mu_L = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.solution:
Since the incident beam is parallel and the emergent beam is also parallel, the two lenses form an afocal system. This means their principal foci coincide, and the distance between them is $d = f_1 + f_2$.

The marginal rays of the beam form similar triangles with the principal axis, with their common vertex at the shared focal point.

From the properties of similar triangles, the ratio of the transverse beam widths is equal to the ratio of the focal lengths of the respective lenses:
$\dfrac{w_2}{w_1} = \dfrac{f_2}{f_1}$

Substituting the given values:
$\dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{f_2}{20}$
$f_2 = 50 \text{ cm}$

The distance between the two lenses is:
$d = f_1 + f_2 = 20 + 50 = 70 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: $70 \text{ cm}$

First, calculate the refractive index of the prism ($\mu_p$) using the minimum deviation condition in air:

$\mu_p = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

In the reflected light, two consecutive missing wavelengths (minimum intensity) are found to be $700\text{ nm}$ and $420\text{ nm}$. The thickness of the transparent film is:
questions.question: A transparent film of refractive index $1.4$ is coated on a glass plate of refractive index $1.5$. White light is incident normally on the film. In the reflected light, two consecutive missing wavelengths (minimum intensity) are found to be $700\text{ nm}$ and $420\text{ nm}$. The thickness of the transparent film is:
questions.solution:
When light reflects from the air-film interface (refractive index $1.0$ to $1.4$), it undergoes a phase change of $\pi$.

When light reflects from the film-glass interface (refractive index $1.4$ to $1.5$), it also reflects from a denser medium, so it undergoes another phase change of $\pi$.

The relative phase shift between the two reflected waves is $0$.

The condition for missing wavelengths (destructive interference) in reflected light with zero relative phase shift is:
$2\mu t = \left(m + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda$
where $m = 0, 1, 2, \dots$

For the two consecutive missing wavelengths $\lambda_1 = 700\text{ nm}$ and $\lambda_2 = 420\text{ nm}$:
$2\mu t = \left(m + 0.5\right) \times 700$
$2\mu t = \left(m + 1.5\right) \times 420$

Equating the two expressions:
$700m + 350 = 420m + 630$
$280m = 280 \Rightarrow m = 1$

Substitute $m = 1$ back into the condition:
$2(1.4)t = (1 + 0.5) \times 700$
$2.8t = 1.5 \times 700 = 1050$
$t = \dfrac{1050}{2.8} = 375\text{ nm}$

Answer: $375\text{ nm}$

$d' = \dfrac{d}{\mu} = \dfrac{24\text{ cm}}{1.5} = 16\text{ cm}$

Let the distance between the lens and the mirror be $d$.
$d + R = v$
$d + 20 = 30$
$d = 10 \text{ cm}$

The curved surface of the right lens is silvered. If an object is placed at a distance of $12$ cm to the left of this optical system, the magnification of the final image is :
questions.solution:
The system acts as an equivalent mirror. First, we find the equivalent power of the unsilvered composite lens $P_L$.

Power of the left plano-convex lens :
$P_1 = (\mu_1 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} \right) = (1.5 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{20} \right) = \dfrac{0.5}{20} = \dfrac{1}{40}$ cm$^{-1}$.

Power of the right plano-convex lens (unsilvered) :
$P_2 = (\mu_2 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right) = (1.6 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{16} \right) = \dfrac{0.6}{16} = \dfrac{3}{80}$ cm$^{-1}$.

Equivalent power of the lens combination :
$P_L = P_1 + P_2 = \dfrac{1}{40} + \dfrac{3}{80} = \dfrac{5}{80} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ cm$^{-1}$.

The silvered curved surface of the right lens acts as a concave mirror with radius $R = 16$ cm. Its power is :
$P_M = \dfrac{2}{R} = \dfrac{2}{16} = \dfrac{1}{8}$ cm$^{-1}$.

The equivalent power of the silvered lens system is :
$P_{eq} = 2P_L + P_M = 2 \left( \dfrac{1}{16} \right) + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}$ cm$^{-1}$.

The system behaves as a concave mirror with an equivalent focal length $F_{eq} = -\dfrac{1}{P_{eq}} = -4$ cm.

Given the object distance $u = -12$ cm, we use the mirror formula :
$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{F_{eq}}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{-12} = -\dfrac{1}{4}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1 - 3}{12} = -\dfrac{2}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{6}$ cm$^{-1}$.
Thus, $v = -6$ cm.

The magnification for the equivalent mirror is :
$m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{-6}{-12} = -0.5$.

It is observed that the image of the object coincides with the object itself when it is at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ from the lens. The refractive index of the liquid is:
questions.solution:
For the image to coincide with the object (auto-collimation), the rays from the object must strike the plane mirror normally. This implies that the rays must emerge parallel to the principal axis after passing through the combination of the glass lens and the liquid lens.

Therefore, the object must be placed at the focal point of the equivalent lens combination. Thus, the equivalent focal length of the combination is $F_{eq} = 30\text{ cm} = 0.3\text{ m}$.

The equivalent power of the lens combination is:
$P_{eq} = \dfrac{1}{F_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{0.3} = \dfrac{10}{3}\text{ D}$

$P_g = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$
$P_g = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{0.2} - \dfrac{1}{-0.2}\right) = 0.5 \times 10 = 5\text{ D}$

$5(\mu_l - 1) = \dfrac{5}{3}$

$\mu_l = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$\left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)F = 10$
$\dfrac{5F}{6} = 10 \Rightarrow F = 12\text{ cm}$.

questions.solution:
The refractive index $\mu$ of a prism is given by the formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + \delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Given that the angle of minimum deviation $\delta_m = A$, we substitute this into the formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin A}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Using the double angle identity $\sin A = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$, we get:

$\mu = \dfrac{2\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\mu = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$

$L_i = m_L \times L_o$
$L_i = \dfrac{4}{25} \times 2\text{ mm} = \dfrac{8}{25}\text{ mm} = 0.32\text{ mm}$

$f = 30 \text{ cm}$

Substitute $\mu_g = 1.5$ and $\mu_l = 1.25$:

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{f_l} = (1.2 - 1) \times \dfrac{1}{10} = 0.2 \times \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{50} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

$\mu_2 = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Let the radii of curvature of the original biconvex lens be $R_1$ and $R_2$.

When cut by a plane perpendicular to the principal axis, the lens is divided into two plano-convex lenses with radii of curvature ($R_1$, $\infty$) and ($\infty$, $R_2$).

The powers of these pieces in air are:
$P_1 = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}\right) = 3\text{ D}$
$P_2 = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-R_2}\right) = 5\text{ D}$

The power of the original uncut lens in air is the sum of the powers of the two pieces:
$P_{\text{air}} = P_1 + P_2 = 3 + 5 = 8\text{ D}$

Using the lens maker's formula for the original lens in air:
$P_{\text{air}} = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) = 8$
$\Rightarrow (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) = 8$
$\Rightarrow \left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) = \dfrac{8}{0.5} = 16\text{ m}^{-1}$

$P_{\text{liquid}} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$
$P_{\text{liquid}} = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{4/3} - 1\right) \times 16$
$P_{\text{liquid}} = \left(\dfrac{9}{8} - 1\right) \times 16 = \dfrac{1}{8} \times 16 = 2\text{ D}$

Answer: $2\text{ D}$

Given that the angle of minimum deviation $\delta_m = 2A$, we substitute this into the formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A+2A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{3A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Using the triple angle identity $\sin(3x) = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$ with $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$:

$\mu = \dfrac{3\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) - 4\sin^3\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\mu = 3 - 4\sin^2\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$

Using the half-angle formula $2\sin^2\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = 1 - \cos A$, we get:

$\mu = 3 - 2(1 - \cos A) = 1 + 2\cos A$

Answer: $1 + 2\cos A$

questions.solution:
Let the side length of the structure be $x$, the focal length be $f$, and the instantaneous height of the drone be $H$.
For a distant object, the image distance $v \approx f$. The linear magnification $m$ is given by:
$m = \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{f}{H}$
where $y$ is the side length of the image on the sensor.

Thus, $y = \dfrac{x f}{H}$

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$:
$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = x f \left( -\dfrac{1}{H^2} \right) \dfrac{dH}{dt}$

$x = 100 \text{ m}$
$f = 10 \text{ cm} = 0.1 \text{ m}$
$H = 1 \text{ km} = 1000 \text{ m}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 100 \times 0.1 \times \left( -\dfrac{1}{(1000)^2} \right) \times (-5)$
$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{10 \times 5}{10^6} \text{ m/s} = 50 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m/s}$

Since $1 \, \mu\text{m} = 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, the rate of increase is $50 \, \mu\text{m/s}$.

Answer: $50 \, \mu\text{m/s}$

The rod is positioned such that its real image spans the exact same segment of the principal axis as the rod itself. If the midpoint of the rod is at a distance of $45\text{ cm}$ from the pole of the mirror, the length of the rod is ______ $\text{cm}$.
questions.solution:
Let the coordinates of the two ends of the rod be $u_A$ and $u_B$.

For the image to span the exact same segment as the object, the image of end A must form at end B, and the image of end B must form at end A. This implies that $u_A$ and $u_B$ are conjugate positions.

Using the mirror formula:
$\dfrac{1}{u_A} + \dfrac{1}{u_B} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

The focal length of the concave mirror is $f = -20\text{ cm}$.
The midpoint of the rod is at $45\text{ cm}$ from the pole, so:
$\dfrac{u_A + u_B}{2} = -45 \Rightarrow u_A + u_B = -90\text{ cm}$

Substituting this into the mirror formula rearranged as $\dfrac{u_A + u_B}{u_A u_B} = \dfrac{1}{f}$:
$\dfrac{-90}{u_A u_B} = \dfrac{1}{-20}$
$u_A u_B = 1800$

The length of the rod is $L = |u_A - u_B|$.
Using the algebraic identity $(u_A - u_B)^2 = (u_A + u_B)^2 - 4u_A u_B$:
$L = \sqrt{(-90)^2 - 4(1800)}$
$L = \sqrt{8100 - 7200} = \sqrt{900} = 30\text{ cm}$.

Answer: $30$

$\dfrac{1}{20} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \mu - 1 = 0.5$
$\Rightarrow \mu = 1.5$

Therefore, $10\mu = 10 \times 1.5 = 15$.

Which of the following is the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum ($400\text{ nm}$ to $700\text{ nm}$) that is maximally transmitted?
questions.solution:
When light reflects from the air-oil interface (refractive index $1.0$ to $1.5$), it undergoes a phase change of $\pi$.

When light reflects from the oil-water interface (refractive index $1.5$ to $1.33$), it reflects from a rarer medium, so there is no phase change.

The relative phase shift between the two reflected waves is $\pi$.

For maximum transmission, the reflected light must undergo destructive interference (minimum intensity).

The condition for destructive interference in reflected light with a relative phase shift of $\pi$ is:
$2\mu t = m\lambda$
where $m = 1, 2, 3, \dots$

Given $\mu = 1.5$ and $t = 600\text{ nm}$:
$2(1.5)(600) = m\lambda$
$1800 = m\lambda$

Checking integer values for $m$:
For $m = 1$, $\lambda = 1800\text{ nm}$
For $m = 2$, $\lambda = 900\text{ nm}$
For $m = 3$, $\lambda = 600\text{ nm}$
For $m = 4$, $\lambda = 450\text{ nm}$

The wavelengths in the visible spectrum ($400\text{ nm}$ to $700\text{ nm}$) are $600\text{ nm}$ and $450\text{ nm}$. The longest among these is $600\text{ nm}$.

Answer: $600\text{ nm}$

The image distance is $v = -4(-15) = +60\text{ cm}$.
Since the object is in front of the mirror and the virtual image is formed behind the mirror, they are on opposite sides of the pole.
The physical distance between them is $|u| + |v| = 15 + 60 = 75\text{ cm}$.

Let the Lens Maker's formula for air be:
$\dfrac{1}{f_a} = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Dividing the two equations:
$\dfrac{f_l}{f_a} = \dfrac{\mu_g - 1}{\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1}$

$\dfrac{24}{12} = \dfrac{1.5 - 1}{\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} - 1}$

$2 = \dfrac{0.5}{\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} - 1}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} - 1 = 0.25$

$\dfrac{1.5}{\mu_l} = 1.25$

$\mu_l = \dfrac{1.5}{1.25} = \dfrac{6}{5}$

Given that $\mu_l = \dfrac{x}{5}$, we get $x = 6$.

If the final image is formed at a distance of $40 \text{ cm}$ in front of the lens, the distance of the original object from the lens is ____ $\text{cm}$.

Let us trace the image formation backwards. The final image is formed after the second refraction through the lens at a distance of $40 \text{ cm}$ in front of it. By sign convention, $v_2 = -40 \text{ cm}$.

$\dfrac{1}{-40} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\dfrac{1}{u_2} = -\dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{1}{20} = -\dfrac{3}{40}$
$u_2 = -\dfrac{40}{3} \text{ cm}$

The distance of this first image from the lens is:
$v_1 = 10 + \dfrac{70}{3} = \dfrac{100}{3} \text{ cm}$

Applying the lens formula for the first refraction to find the original object distance $u_1$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{3}{100} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{3}{100} - \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{3 - 5}{100} = -\dfrac{2}{100} = -\dfrac{1}{50}$
$u_1 = -50 \text{ cm}$

When the ray is incident at the exact critical angle for total internal reflection, the angle between the incident ray and the internally reflected ray is found to be $106^\circ$. questions.question: A light ray travelling in a transparent glass block of refractive index $1.5$ strikes a planar boundary with a liquid of refractive index $n$. When the ray is incident at the exact critical angle for total internal reflection, the angle between the incident ray and the internally reflected ray is found to be $106^\circ$. If $\sin(53^\circ) = \dfrac{4}{5}$, the value of $10n$ is ________.
questions.solution:
According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.

Given the angle between the incident ray and the internally reflected ray is $106^\circ$, the angle of incidence is $i = \dfrac{106^\circ}{2} = 53^\circ$.

For the critical angle condition, the refracted ray grazes the boundary, so the angle of refraction is $90^\circ$.

Applying Snell's law at the glass-liquid interface:
$\mu_{\text{glass}} \sin i = n \sin 90^\circ$

$1.5 \times \sin 53^\circ = n \times 1$

$1.5 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = n$

$n = 1.2$

Therefore, $10n = 10 \times 1.2 = 12$.

Answer: $12$

questions.question: A short linear pin of length $2.0\text{ mm}$ lies along the principal axis of a convex spherical boundary separating air (refractive index $1$) and glass (refractive index $1.5$). The radius of curvature of the spherical boundary is $10\text{ cm}$. If the center of the pin is at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ from the pole in air, the length of the image formed inside the glass is:
questions.solution:
Given:
Refractive index of air, $n_1 = 1$
Refractive index of glass, $n_2 = 1.5$
Radius of curvature, $R = +10\text{ cm}$
Object distance, $u = -30\text{ cm}$
Length of the object, $du = 2.0\text{ mm}$

Using the formula for refraction at a single spherical surface:
$\dfrac{n_2}{v} - \dfrac{n_1}{u} = \dfrac{n_2 - n_1}{R}$

Substituting the values:
$\dfrac{1.5}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1.5 - 1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{v} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{0.5}{10} = \dfrac{1.5}{30}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{v} = \dfrac{1.5}{30} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{0.5}{30}$

$v = 90\text{ cm}$

For a short linear object along the principal axis, the longitudinal magnification $m_L$ is obtained by differentiating the refraction formula:
$-\dfrac{n_2}{v^2} dv + \dfrac{n_1}{u^2} du = 0$

$m_L = \left| \dfrac{dv}{du} \right| = \dfrac{n_1}{n_2} \left( \dfrac{v}{u} \right)^2$

$m_L = \dfrac{1}{1.5} \times \left( \dfrac{90}{-30} \right)^2 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 9 = 6$

Length of the image $= m_L \times du = 6 \times 2.0\text{ mm} = 12.0\text{ mm}$

Answer: $12.0\text{ mm}$

questions.question: A convex lens forms a virtual image of an object which is $3$ times the size of the object. If the distance between the object and its image is $20\text{ cm}$, the focal length of the lens is :
questions.solution:
For a convex lens forming a virtual image, the image is erect and formed on the same side as the object.

Given magnification $m = +3$.
We know that $m = \dfrac{v}{u} = 3 \Rightarrow v = 3u$.

Since both the object and the virtual image are on the same side of the lens, and the image is magnified ($|v| > |u|$), the distance between them is given by:
$|v| - |u| = 20$
$-v - (-u) = 20$
$-3u + u = 20$
$-2u = 20 \Rightarrow u = -10\text{ cm}$

Then, $v = 3(-10) = -30\text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-30} - \dfrac{1}{-10}$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{-1 + 3}{30} = \dfrac{2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{15}$

$\Rightarrow f = 15\text{ cm}$

Answer: $15\text{ cm}$

If the speed of light in the material of the prism is $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$, the angle of the prism (in degrees) is _______. questions.question: The graph of angle of deviation $\delta$ versus angle of incidence $i$ for a transparent prism shows that the minimum deviation occurs when the angle of incidence is exactly equal to the angle of the prism. If the speed of light in the material of the prism is $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$, the angle of the prism (in degrees) is _______. (Take the speed of light in vacuum as $3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$)
questions.solution:
The refractive index of the prism is given by:
$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \times 10^8} = \sqrt{2}$

At minimum deviation, the angle of incidence $i$ is equal to the angle of emergence $e$. The deviation is given by:
$\delta_{\min} = 2i - A$

We are given that minimum deviation occurs when $i = A$. Substituting this:
$\delta_{\min} = 2A - A = A$

Using the prism formula:
$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + \delta_{\min}}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin(A)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Using the double angle identity $\sin(A) = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$:
$\sqrt{2} = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$

$\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\dfrac{A}{2} = 45^\circ$

$A = 90^\circ$

Answer: $90$

A point object is placed on the principal axis in front of the lens such that its final image coincides with the object itself, irrespective of the distance between the lens and the mirror. The distance of the object from the lens is _____ $\text{cm}$.
questions.solution:
Using the Lens Maker's formula for the lens immersed in the liquid:
$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Given $\mu_g = 1.5$, $\mu_l = 1.25$, $R_1 = 20\text{ cm}$, and $R_2 = -20\text{ cm}$ (for a biconvex lens):
$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.25} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{-20}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = (1.2 - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = 0.2 \times \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{50}$

$f_l = 50\text{ cm}$

For the final image to coincide with the object irrespective of the plane mirror's position, the light rays emerging from the lens must be parallel to the principal axis. This ensures they strike the plane mirror normally and retrace their path.

This condition is satisfied when the object is placed at the principal focus of the lens in the liquid.

Therefore, the object distance from the lens is equal to its focal length in the liquid, which is $50\text{ cm}$.

$\mu = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{2}}{1/2} = \sqrt{2}$

Given that $\mu = \sqrt{x}$, we have $\sqrt{x} = \sqrt{2}$, which gives $x = 2$.

After emerging from the prism, the ray strikes a plane mirror. The mirror is oriented such that the reflected ray becomes anti-parallel to the original incident ray. questions.solution:
For the prism, the angle $A = 60^\circ$ and refractive index $\mu = \sqrt{3}$.
At minimum deviation, the angle of refraction inside the prism is $r = \dfrac{A}{2} = 30^\circ$.

Using Snell's law at the first surface:
$1 \times \sin(i) = \mu \sin(r)$
$\sin(i) = \sqrt{3} \sin(30^\circ) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$i = 60^\circ$

The deviation produced by the prism is:
$\delta_p = 2i - A = 2(60^\circ) - 60^\circ = 60^\circ$

For the final reflected ray to be anti-parallel to the original incident ray, the total deviation of the ray must be $180^\circ$.
Let the deviation produced by the plane mirror be $\delta_m$. Since the deviations are in the same sense:
$\delta_p + \delta_m = 180^\circ$
$60^\circ + \delta_m = 180^\circ$
$\delta_m = 120^\circ$

The deviation produced by a plane mirror is related to the angle of incidence $\phi$ on the mirror by:
$\delta_m = 180^\circ - 2\phi$
$120^\circ = 180^\circ - 2\phi$
$2\phi = 60^\circ$
$\phi = 30^\circ$

Answer: $30$
